role: Business Intelligence Engineer II, CDR Pillar 1 Strategy and DX
responsibilities: Design, develop and maintain scaled, automated, user-friendly systems, reports, dashboards, etc. that will support the needs of the business.
Collaborate with internal program and product owners, engineering teams to improve distributed and Supply Chain Management Systems Data.
Apply deep analytic and business intelligence skills to extract meaningful insights and learning from large and complicated data sets.
Design, develop, and maintain scalable and reliable data pipelines for optimal extraction, transformation, and loading of data from diverse sources using SQL, Python, and AWS big data technologies.

Design and implement master data management frameworks, including data governance, data quality standards, deduplication, enrichment, and synchronization of master data entities such as Product Master, Vendor Master, Location Master, Item Master, and Bill of Materials.
Enhance analytical maturity by incorporating predictive and prescriptive analytics using machine learning and optimization techniques where appropriate.

Oversee and continually improve internal customer experience, production operations, including optimizing data delivery, redesigning infrastructure for greater scalability, managing code deployments, resolving bugs, and coordinating overall release management.
Establish and maintain best practices for design, development, and support of data integration solutions, including comprehensive documentation.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Governance, data quality, integrity and reliable pipelines recur throughout, against a single "fast-paced, dynamic environment", so rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: generating insights to help senior leaders make critical business decisions
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Supply chain data for AWS infrastructure informs business decisions, with no financial-reporting or regulatory language, so moderate.
evidence.collaboration_width: internal program and product owners; engineering teams; senior leaders
evidence.data_team_maturity: join a growing analytics team within Amazon
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The hire will "join a growing analytics team within Amazon" and "Enhance analytical maturity", so the data function exists and is still growing.
evidence.jd_authorship: synchronization of master data entities such as Product Master, Vendor Master, Location Master, Item Master, and Bill of Materials
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name the master data entities, pipeline stack and release duties precisely, so a reader can picture the work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: building visualizations and tools for our business partners
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role splits between supply chain business partners and senior leaders on one side and internal data work (master data, pipelines, release management) on the other, so mixed.
evidence.autonomy_level: Establish and maintain best practices for design, development, and support of data integration solutions
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The hire sets master data and integration standards ("Establish and maintain best practices") while also building reports for business needs, so mixed.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: Machine learning appears only as predictive analytics, with no AI tool use or AI-facing data work expected.
evidence.testing_framing: Design and implement master data management frameworks, including data governance, data quality standards
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data quality standards and governance are framed as frameworks the hire designs and implements, so responsibility.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: govern the integrity of critical supply chain data entities
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Data integrity and governance sit in the role summary and recur in responsibilities and qualifications, so trust in the data dominates the framing.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The dominant verbs improve, redesign and scale existing supply chain data systems as part of a transformation programme.
evidence.loss_aversion: implementing master data management frameworks that govern the integrity of critical supply chain data entities — the role exists to keep master data trustworthy.
ats_keywords: Redshift, S3, AWS Glue, EMR, Kinesis
